skill.name: sbom-syft
skill.description: Guides Syft-based SBOM generation for container images, filesystems, and archives. Covers CycloneDX, SPDX, CI integration, vulnerability workflows, and signed attestations.
skill.summary: Generate and manage Syft SBOMs for software supply chain visibility.
skill.author: AgentSecOps

security_audit.summary: Most detections are false positives caused by Markdown formatting, defensive examples, or fixed local operations. The template still includes a critical pipe-to-shell installer and instructions that download mutable artifacts without integrity verification. It also exposes a GitHub token to an unpinned action and contains CI controls that can fail open.

remediation.issue: Remote script is piped directly into bash.
remediation.suggestion: Install tfsec from a pinned release, then verify its checksum or signature before execution.

remediation.issue: CI actions, images, and downloaded binaries use mutable references.
remediation.suggestion: Pin actions and images by immutable digest, and pin release versions with published integrity verification.

remediation.issue: Scanner failures and findings can be ignored by the pipeline.
remediation.suggestion: Separate scanner errors from findings, enforce the configured threshold, and fail when required reports are missing.

remediation.issue: Registry credentials are shown in a project configuration file.
remediation.suggestion: Use a credential helper or CI secret injection, and exclude local secret configuration from version control.

content.value_statement: Manual software inventories are incomplete and difficult to maintain. This skill guides repeatable Syft SBOM generation for containers, filesystems, archives, and CI pipelines.
actual_capabilities: Select Syft targets for container images, directories, and OCI or Docker archives.
Generate CycloneDX, SPDX, Syft JSON, and human-readable SBOM outputs.
Configure catalog scope, archive scanning, exclusions, and default output formats.
Integrate SBOM generation into GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, and Jenkins workflows.
Connect generated SBOMs to Grype scanning, license review, and cosign attestations.
limitations: Requires an installed Syft binary or a working Docker environment.
Finds only packages visible to Syft and accessible within the selected target.
Does not replace vulnerability triage, license counsel, or provenance verification.
Included CI and installation examples require security hardening before production use.

use_cases.title: Inventory Release Images
use_cases.description: Generate CycloneDX and SPDX inventories for each container release and retain them with build artifacts.

use_cases.title: Automate Build Evidence
use_cases.description: Add repeatable SBOM generation, validation, and artifact retention to an existing delivery pipeline.

use_cases.title: Review Dependency Licenses
use_cases.description: Extract package and license data for compliance review across applications and container images.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Container SBOM
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a CycloneDX SBOM for <container-image>. Confirm the target, choose a safe output path, and explain how to validate the result.

prompt_templates.title: Scan a Project Directory
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate an SPDX SBOM for <project-path>. Exclude <patterns>, report detected ecosystems, and identify likely coverage gaps.

prompt_templates.title: Add SBOM Generation to CI
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a CI job for <platform> that generates an SBOM for <artifact>. Pin dependencies, verify tools, retain outputs, and fail on missing reports.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Signed Supply Chain Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan an advanced workflow for <image> that generates multiple SBOM formats, scans vulnerabilities, enforces policy, signs attestations, and verifies published evidence.

output_examples.input: Create a CycloneDX inventory for the release image and retain it for audit.
output: Target confirmed as the immutable release image digest.
CycloneDX output stored with the release artifacts.
Validation checks confirm the file is readable and contains package components.

output_examples.input: Compare dependencies between two application releases and highlight license changes.
output: Added and removed packages are grouped by ecosystem.
Version changes are listed separately from package additions.
New or changed licenses are flagged for compliance review.

output_examples.input: Prepare a secure CI plan for generating and signing an SBOM.
output_examples.output: The plan pins tool sources, verifies downloads, generates the SBOM, enforces scan policy, signs the attestation, and retains verification evidence.

best_practices: Scan immutable image digests and record the matching source revision.
Pin every action, image, and binary, then verify downloaded artifacts before execution.
Store SBOMs as protected release evidence and regenerate them after dependency changes.
anti_patterns: Do not pipe remote installation scripts directly into a shell.
Do not treat an SBOM as proof that software is vulnerability-free or compliant.
Do not store registry credentials in committed Syft configuration files.

faq.question: What targets can this skill inventory?
faq.answer: It covers container images, local filesystems, project directories, and OCI or Docker archives supported by Syft.

faq.question: Which SBOM formats are supported?
faq.answer: The guidance covers CycloneDX JSON and XML, SPDX JSON and tag-value, Syft JSON, and readable text output.

faq.question: Does this skill include Syft?
faq.answer: No. Install a verified Syft release or use a pinned container image before running the documented workflows.

faq.question: Can it find vulnerabilities?
faq.answer: Syft inventories packages. Use Grype or another compatible scanner to evaluate the resulting SBOM for known vulnerabilities.

faq.question: Can it support license compliance?
faq.answer: It can extract reported license data for review. Legal interpretation and policy decisions still require qualified oversight.

faq.question: How should SBOMs be protected?
faq.answer: Restrict access, retain release provenance, avoid exposing internal package details, and verify signatures before trusting published attestations.
